transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-04-11
- Time: 16:00 UTC
- Duration: ~42 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Samir (CSM), Elena (HelioGrid Head of Platform), Tom (ML Eng), Priya (Infra), Ryan (Procurement)

Auto summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
HelioGrid is evaluating a renewal that includes a 6-9 month commitment bump to support increased traffic for their agent orchestration product. Primary asks: Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput, an EU edge region for latency-sensitive EU customers, and confirmation on data residency and compliance docs. Redwood to send SOW with EU edge pricing and provision a short Dedicated trial.

Topics:
- Renewal term and uplift
- EU region onboarding (eu-west-3 vs eu-central-1)
- Dedicated trial and provisioning timeline
- Security/compliance artifacts and network requirements
- Price sensitivity and fallback routing strategy

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call then we'll dive.
[00:12] Elena: Hi yea Elena here.
[00:14] Tom: Tom, hi.
[00:16] Priya: Priya.
[00:18] Ryan: Ryan here.
[00:20] Jordan (SE): Jordan from Redwood.
[00:22] Samir: Samir, CSM.
[00:25] Maya: Cool, couple goals for today — confirm the scale numbers for renew, pick the EU region for edge, and agree on next steps for the Dedicated trial.

[02:10] Elena: Brief context — our traffic spiked after we launched the Helio Agents 2.0 in March. Latency complaints from EU customers up ~30% so we want an EU edge. Also we are leaning towards a 9-month uplift with reserved capacity because bursty inference is hurting costs.

[03:05] Jordan: Understood. For the EU edge we support provisioning in eu-west-3 and eu-central-1. Performance-wise eu-west-3 has slightly better p99 to the customer base you mentioned, but eu-central-1 has different availability windows for some partners.

[04:30] Tom: Is there a big perf delta between the two? we care about p95/p99 more than average.

[04:45] Jordan: Good Q — short answer is p95 is similar, p99 in eu-west-3 on our benchmarks was about 8-12 ms faster for your model family, but that depends on sequence length. we can run a quick tail-latency run in the Dedicated trial.

[06:00] Priya: On networking: we need to know IP ranges, peering options, and whether you can support an on-prem connector. we are locked down on outbound while-inbound flows are restricted.

[06:20] Jordan: We have VPC peering and Transit Gateway options. For Private deployments we also offer an on-prem package but that usually is a longer project. For Dedicated eu edge, we can provide customer-managed VPC peering; Jordan: I'll share the network diagram.

[07:45] Ryan: Pricing — we are comparing reserved vs metered. we have procurement runway of two quarters and need capex predictability. any flexibility on a stepped ramp?

[08:05] Maya: Yes we can do a stepped commit — e.g., 3 months at X, 3 months at Y, rest at Z — that reduces the up-front commitment while giving you guaranteed units. We'll include a ramp table in the SOW.

[09:30] Elena: Also curious about fallback behavior — if Dedicated capacity hits a limit can requests spill to hosted models in another region without exposing customer data?

[10:00] Jordan: We support smart routing with fallbacks to verified model variants; we can keep requests in the same tenancy with encryption in transit, but we need to nail the policy — some customers prefer fail-open with a warning, others want an error. We can set automatic fallback to lower-cost model variants in the same region or route to hosted in a different region with redaction. we'll document options.

[12:20] Tom: On the Dedicated trial, can we test with our KV cache patterns? our workloads do long context agent runs.

[12:40] Jordan: Absolutely — we'll configure KV cache settings and continuous batching similar to your production profile. Ideally you send a representative workload or trace.

[14:05] Priya: Security/compliance — we need SOC 2 Type II, encryption at rest with customer KMS, and audit logs delivered to our SIEM. Are those standard?

[14:25] Samir: Yes we've got SOC 2 and ISO docs. we support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments, for Dedicated we can support CMEK depending on the region. Audit logs can be forwarded to your S3 or a SIEM with a retention policy. I'll attach the docs.

[16:10] Elena: Great. also, we have an internal security questionnaire (60 questions) — how fast can that be returned?

[16:30] Maya: If you share it we can prioritize. Samir: typical turnaround for a standard questionnaire is 3-5 business days, more if there are legal or network deep dives.

[18:00] Ryan: Contract length — we prefer 9 months with a 30-day exit if SLA misses are consistent. Is that ok?

[18:20] Maya: We can accommodate a 9-month term and include SLA credits; the 30-day exit clause is unusual but we can propose a remediation/fix period in the SOW, maybe a 30–60 day remediation window before termination. we'll flag legal for approval.

[20:50] Tom: One question about model variants — do you allow pinning to a quantized variant? we want the cost savings but worried about subtle quality regressions.

[21:05] Jordan: Yes, we support pinned quantized variants and rollbacks. We'll run evals on your prompt set during the trial and set regression alerts. this is part of Redwood Optimize recommendations.

[23:40] Priya: Back to networking: for eu-west-3 we'd need the exact AZ distribution for redundancy planning.

[23:55] Jordan: I'll include AZ details in the network diagram doc. also note Dedicated pools are spread across two AZs by default to meet availability targets.

[26:10] Elena: Are there any competitors that provide a simpler price model? we are hearing from a few vendors that push pure spot-based inference at lower cost but higher variability.

[26:30] Maya: Right — we see solutions that emphasize spot-only to reduce baseline cost but that comes with preemption risk. Our approach is to provide mixed pools and fallback policies; you get cost efficiency without sacrificing SLAs.

[28:00] Ryan: Procurement question: do you accept PO + invoice or do we need a contract signature first?

[28:15] Maya: We accept PO + invoice for existing customers; for net-new terms we usually finalize an SOW and signature. since you're renewing, we can do PO + invoice tied to the SOW.

[30:05] Tom: For the Dedicated trial, can we run our real models or do we need to use sandbox tokens? we prefer realistic load tests.

[30:20] Jordan: You can run real models in a trial Dedicated environment; we'll issue temporary credentials and capacity. We do rate-limit to protect the cluster but it's representative.

[33:00] Elena: Any concerns about multi-tenant data leakage when we route to hosted fallback? we process PII in some prompts.

[33:20] Jordan: Good point. For PII we recommend VPC-only Dedicated or Private deployments. For hosted fallback we can ensure token-level redaction and only route non-sensitive traffic — or configure a strict deny for fallback on endpoints dealing with PII.

[35:10] Priya: On the SSO/SAML side, we need SSO integration for the console and RBAC for token issuance.

[35:25] Samir: We support SAML SSO, SCIM for user provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC. we'll provide a setup guide.

[37:40] Maya: recap — Redwood will: draft SOW with stepped ramp and EU edge pricing, provision a 2-week Dedicated trial in eu-west-3, share SOC2/ISO + network diagram, and stand up KV/cache config for Tom's workload.

[38:05] Elena: HelioGrid will: pick a preferred EU region by 2027-04-14, send the security questionnaire, and provide IP ranges/approval owner.

[39:00] Ryan: We'll also want a sample invoice draft for procurement.

[39:20] Maya: We'll include a sample invoice template in the SOW packet.

[40:00] Jordan: I'll open a temporary ticket and link the Dedicated trial resources; expect credentials ETA 2027-04-18.

[41:00] Maya: Ok thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email and set the follow-up for next week to review trial metrics.
[41:20] Elena: Thanks all.
[41:30] Meeting end.
